title: Counit normalization of exact pullback and its strict completed construction
statement:
Let $g:Y\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], with small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Fix a Noetherian adic datum $(A,I)$, $P_n=A/I^n$ for $n\ge1$, and $B_T=\varprojlim_n(P_n)_T$ for $T=X,Y$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Assume the projection-defined coefficient map $c_g:g^{-1}B_X\to B_Y$ of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] is an isomorphism. Use module sheaves, their unbounded derived categories and strict inverse sequences [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-inverse-system].

Write $G(M)=g^{-1}M\otimes_{g^{-1}B_X,c_g}B_Y$ for the recorded ordinary module pullback, and $F(M)$ for $g^{-1}M$ with scalars transported along $c_g^{-1}$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Let $m:G\xrightarrow{\sim}F$ be the module isomorphism sending $x\otimes b$ to $b\cdot x$. Assume $F$ is additive and exact. Denote its termwise derived descent by $F_D$, with localization comparison $\xi_P:F_D(Q_XP)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_Y(FP)$ [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. Let $L$ be the specified K-flat left-derived pullback of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], with its universal counit $\epsilon_P:L(Q_XP)\to Q_Y(GP)$, where $Q_T$ denotes localization of cochain complexes at quasi-isomorphisms [def-pc-kflat-complex].

There is a unique natural isomorphism $e:L\xrightarrow{\sim}F_D$ satisfying
$$\xi_P e_{Q_XP}=Q_Y(m_P)\epsilon_P$$
for every complex $P$. The corresponding universal-counit-normalized isomorphism on derived strict towers identifies the specified left-derived levelwise pullback with $F_D^{\mathrm{Tow}}$. It agrees with $e$ under every tower evaluation and with $\Delta e$ on constant towers, using the exact-localization comparisons, where $\Delta$ denotes constant towers.

For $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_X))$, let $K_\bullet$ be its strict derived quotient tower. Applying total right derived limit to this tower isomorphism gives an isomorphism $d_K$ from the actual ambient strict completed pullback to $L_YF_D^{\mathrm{Tow}}K_\bullet$, where $L_Y=R\lim$. Let $\alpha_K$ be the actual comparison defined by the strict quotient augmentation in [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], and let $\alpha^F_K:F_DK\to L_YF_D^{\mathrm{Tow}}K_\bullet$ be the same augmented construction with exact termwise $F$. Then
$$d_K\alpha_K=\alpha^F_K e_K.$$
The isomorphism $d_K$ commutes with each derived-limit evaluation through the preceding tower comparison. These assertions hold for every unbounded $K$, using the ambient augmented construction even when $K$ is not intrinsically complete.

proof.text: Put $H(P)=Q_Y(FP)$ and $H_G(P)=Q_Y(GP)$, with the termwise extension of $m$ still denoted $m$. By the exact-functor derived-functor theorem, $(F_D,\xi)$ is a universal left derived pair for $H$. The pair $(L,Q_Y(m)\epsilon)$ is another: composition with the natural isomorphism $Q_Y(m)$ converts, bijectively, transformations into $H_G$ into transformations into $H$, and its inverse converts them back. Apply uniqueness of right Kan extensions to these two pairs. This gives a unique natural isomorphism $e:L\to F_D$ with $\xi_Pe_{Q_XP}=Q_Y(m_P)\epsilon_P$. In particular every $\epsilon_P$ is invertible, since the other three maps in this equation are invertible. This argument uses the specified counit, not just an abstract isomorphism between the functors.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor, and its left-derived dual; universal comparison as in Mathlib CategoryTheory/Functor/KanExtension/Basic.lean rightKanExtensionUnique

proof.text: Write $\mathcal T_T=\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}(B_T))$ and $\widetilde L$ for the specified left-derived levelwise $G$, with counit $\tau$. Kernels and cokernels in $\mathcal T_T$ are levelwise. Hence levelwise $F$, written $F^{\mathrm{Tow}}$, is additive and exact: evaluation of its kernel or cokernel comparison is the corresponding isomorphism for $F$. Likewise $m$ gives a natural isomorphism $m^{\mathrm{Tow}}:G^{\mathrm{Tow}}\to F^{\mathrm{Tow}}$, since its components commute with every tower transition by naturality of $m$. Apply the two cited universal comparison results to the abelian categories $\mathcal T_X,\mathcal T_Y$. They give a unique $E:\widetilde L\xrightarrow{\sim}F_D^{\mathrm{Tow}}$ with $\Xi_M E_{Q M}=Q(m^{\mathrm{Tow}}_M)\tau_M$ for every complex of strict towers $M$, where $\Xi$ is exact localization comparison. In particular this is a comparison in the derived category of strict towers.

source.place: Tag 015F applied to the abelian strict-tower categories; homology.tex Tag 02MZ, lemma-inverse-systems-abelian; right Kan extension uniqueness

proof.text: Use the counit-normalized evaluation comparisons $v_n:\operatorname{ev}_n\widetilde L\cong L\operatorname{ev}_n$. On an objectwise K-flat flat-term representative $M$, the equation for $E$ evaluates to $Q(m_{M_n})\operatorname{ev}_n(\tau_M)$. The equation for $e$ after $v_n$ is $Q(m_{M_n})\epsilon_{M_n}v_n$, equal to that expression by the defining equation $\epsilon_{M_n}v_n=\operatorname{ev}_n(\tau_M)$. Thus evaluation of $E$ is $e\operatorname{ev}_n$ after $v_n$ and the exact-localization comparisons. Every derived strict tower has such a representative by the strict diagram replacement theorem; these equalities therefore hold on every object by naturality along its replacement isomorphism. The $v_n$ commute with transitions by the cited evaluation theorem, so these identifications respect all transitions as well.

source.place: Tag 06XN, lemma-find-existence-computes, dual; normalized evaluation equation of lem-cbc-derived-tower-evaluation-normalization

proof.text: Let $b:\Delta_YL\xrightarrow{\sim}\widetilde L\Delta_X$ be the counit-normalized constant-tower comparison. Let $c:\Delta_YF_D\xrightarrow{\sim}F_D^{\mathrm{Tow}}\Delta_X$ be the comparison obtained from the identity $\Delta_YF=F^{\mathrm{Tow}}\Delta_X$ on complexes by exact localization. Constant towers are exact because kernels and cokernels are levelwise. We have $E_{\Delta K}b_K=c_K\Delta_Y(e_K)$. To check it, represent $K$ by a K-flat flat-term $P$. Compose both sides with the target exact-localization comparison $\Xi_{\Delta P}$. The first becomes $Q(m_{\Delta P})\tau_{\Delta P}b_{Q P}=\Delta_Y(Q(m_P)\epsilon_P)$ by normalization of $b$. The second is the same expression by the defining equation for $e$, since $m_{\Delta P}=\Delta_Ym_P$. Cancel $\Xi_{\Delta P}$. Naturality along a K-flat replacement proves the equation for every $K$. This verifies the constant-tower compatibility in the strict derived tower category, without testing equality merely on its evaluations.

source.place: Tag 06XN, lemma-find-existence-computes, dual; counit normalization of constant towers; Tag 015F for exact localization

proof.text:
For any $K$, choose a K-flat flat-term representative $P$ and write $R(P)_n=P\otimes_{B_X}(P_n)_X$ and $a_P:\Delta_XP\to R(P)$ for $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. Thus $K_\bullet=Q R(P)$. Write $a_K:\Delta_XK\to K_\bullet$ for this localized augmentation. The actual pulled-back augmentation is $\beta_K=\widetilde L(a_K)b_K:\Delta_YLK\to\widetilde L K_\bullet$, and the exact one is $\beta^F_K=F_D^{\mathrm{Tow}}(a_K)c_K:\Delta_YF_DK\to F_D^{\mathrm{Tow}}K_\bullet$. Indeed the strict quotient computation gives the actual representative $w_P=\widetilde L(Qa_P)\tau_{\Delta P}^{-1}$; after identifying $LK$ with $QG(P)$ by $\epsilon_P$, this is precisely $\beta_K$, because $\tau_{\Delta P}b_{Q P}=\Delta_Y\epsilon_P$. These formulas are compatible with changing K-flat representatives by the same cited computation. Naturality of $E$ at $a_K$ and Step 4 now give explicitly
$$E_{K_\bullet}\beta_K=F_D^{\mathrm{Tow}}(a_K)E_{\Delta K}b_K=F_D^{\mathrm{Tow}}(a_K)c_K\Delta_Y(e_K)=\beta^F_K\Delta_Y(e_K).$$
No K-flatness of the quotient levels is used.

source.place: Strict quotient augmentation of def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback; Stacks Tag 06XN for resolving the quotient diagram; agent-written naturality square

proof.text:
Let $L_Y=R\lim$ be the total right derived inverse-limit functor and put $d_K=L_Y(E_{K_\bullet})$. It is an isomorphism, since a functor sends an inverse pair to an inverse pair. Use the normalized adjunction $\Delta_Y\dashv L_Y$ with unit $u_C:C\to L_Y\Delta_YC$. The ambient construction in the completed-pullback definition is $\alpha_K=L_Y(\beta_K)u_{LK}$; the exact augmented construction is $\alpha^F_K=L_Y(\beta^F_K)u_{F_DK}$. These are exactly the chain-level compatible-map constructions: for a tower K-injective resolution of $\Delta_YC$, the adjunction unit is the map into its termwise limit induced by the compatible resolution maps. Apply $L_Y$ to Step 5 and use the unit's naturality $L_Y(\Delta_Ye_K)u_{LK}=u_{F_DK}e_K$. This yields
$$d_K\alpha_K=L_Y(E_{K_\bullet}\beta_K)u_{LK}=L_Y(\beta^F_K)L_Y(\Delta_Ye_K)u_{LK}=\alpha^F_Ke_K.$$
Both sides of this equality are the specified augmented maps.

proof.text:
For the natural derived-limit projections $\pi_{n,M}:L_YM\to\operatorname{ev}_nM$, apply the naturality asserted in the normalized tower-counit theorem to $E_{K_\bullet}$. It gives
$$\pi_{n,F_D^{\mathrm{Tow}}K_\bullet}d_K=\operatorname{ev}_n(E_{K_\bullet})\pi_{n,\widetilde L K_\bullet}.$$
Step 3 identifies the evaluated map with the prescribed ordinary comparison $e$ and $v_n$. This is the claimed derived-limit evaluation compatibility. All replacements and functors used above exist on unbounded complexes. The quotient augmentation, $\beta_K$, and $L_Y\beta_K\,u$ make sense for every $K$; completeness is needed only to restrict the completed-pullback functor to its intrinsic complete subcategory, not for any of these constructions or equalities. In particular the argument never identifies an arbitrary map of triangulated cones with the augmentation.
